_comment: Owner-curated confusable pairs. The engine may ONLY post pairs from this list — the LLM never invents a pair. 'rule' is the verified one-line distinction the post is written from. Add pairs freely; keep each rule true and short.

pairs.rule: affect is usually the verb (to influence); effect is usually the noun (the result).
accept = to receive or agree; except = excluding.
advice is the noun; advise is the verb.
adapt = change to fit; adopt = take as your own.
allusion = an indirect reference; illusion = a false impression.
altar = a table in a place of worship; alter = to change.
amoral = without any sense of right and wrong; immoral = knowingly wrong.
beside = next to; besides = in addition to.
breath is the noun; breathe is the verb.
canvas = strong cloth; canvass = to ask people for votes or opinions.
capital = main city or money; Capitol = a specific government building (US).
censor = remove objectionable parts; censure = formally criticise.
cite = quote as evidence; site = a place or location.
climactic relates to a climax; climatic relates to climate.
complement = completes something; compliment = praise.
conscience = inner sense of right and wrong; conscious = awake or aware.
continual = repeated with breaks; continuous = without any break.
council = an official group; counsel = advice, or to advise.
credible = believable; credulous = too ready to believe.
deprecate = express disapproval; depreciate = lose value.
desert = dry land, or to abandon; dessert = sweet course after a meal.
discreet = careful not to attract attention; discrete = separate, distinct.
disinterested = impartial; uninterested = not interested.
elicit = draw out a response; illicit = illegal.
eligible = qualified; illegible = impossible to read.
emigrate = leave your country; immigrate = come into a new country.
eminent = famous and respected; imminent = about to happen.
ensure = make certain; insure = protect with an insurance policy.
envelop (verb) = wrap or surround; envelope (noun) = paper cover for a letter.
exalt = praise highly or raise in rank; exult = rejoice triumphantly.
explicit = stated clearly; implicit = suggested, not stated.
farther = physical distance; further = extent or degree, or additional.
fewer with things you can count; less with things you cannot count.
flaunt = show off; flout = openly break a rule.
forward = ahead; foreword = a short introduction at the start of a book.
historic = important in history; historical = related to the past.
human = of people; humane = kind and compassionate.
the speaker implies (suggests); the listener infers (concludes).
incredible = unbelievable; incredulous = unwilling to believe.
industrial = relating to industry; industrious = hard-working.
ingenious = clever and inventive; ingenuous = innocent and trusting.
lay needs an object (lay the book down); lie does not (lie down).
loath (adjective) = unwilling; loathe (verb) = hate.
loose = not tight; lose = fail to keep or to win.
luxuriant = growing thickly (luxuriant hair); luxurious = expensive and comfortable.
moral = about right and wrong; morale = confidence and spirit of a group.
official = authorised; officious = bossy, interfering.
passed is the past tense of pass; past = time before now, or beyond.
personal = private, your own; personnel = the staff of an organisation.
perspective = point of view; prospective = likely to be in the future.
precede = come before; proceed = go on or continue.
prescribe = recommend or order; proscribe = forbid.
principal = main, or head of a school; principle = a basic rule or belief.
prophecy is the noun (a prediction); prophesy is the verb.
quiet = silent; quite = fairly or completely.
respectful = showing respect; respective = belonging to each one separately.
sensible = practical, reasonable; sensitive = easily affected or upset.
stationary = not moving; stationery = paper, pens and office supplies.
than compares; then refers to time.
tortuous = full of twists; torturous = causing great pain.
urban = of a city; urbane = polished and courteous.
venal = open to bribery; venial = minor and forgivable.
waive = give up a right or fee; wave = move the hand, or a moving ridge of water.
wander = walk without a fixed route; wonder = think curiously, or amazement.
weather = rain, sun and so on; whether introduces a choice or doubt.
childish = immature (negative); childlike = innocent (positive).
economic = relating to the economy; economical = not wasteful, saving money.
classic = excellent of its kind, typical; classical = relating to ancient Greece/Rome or traditional art music.
parts compose the whole; the whole comprises the parts.
elusive = hard to find or catch; illusive = deceptive, not real.
judicial = relating to courts; judicious = showing good judgement.
militate (against) = work against; mitigate = make less severe.
popular = liked by many; populous = having many people.
a person is regretful (feels sorry); an event is regrettable (deserves regret).
sceptic = a doubter; septic = infected.
stimulant = a substance that increases activity; stimulus = anything that causes a reaction.
vocation = a calling or career; vacation = a holiday.
